body:
You are drafting spoken lines for a video game. Reply with plain text only, in the exact row format given at the end of this message. Do not send messages to anyone else and do not ask questions: decide. Write nothing but the rows (no title, no notes, no Markdown).

THE GAME. "The Crooked Moon" is a single-player, turn-based tactical party RPG built from a folk-horror Dungeons and Dragons campaign. It is set in Wickermoor Hollow, a haunted valley in Druskenvald, a land of endless night under a giant Crooked Moon with a crone's face. The look is a Halloween that never ends, drawn like an 1980s cartoon. A ghost train, the Ghostlight Express, has crashed in the valley; the party is stranded in the Hollow and its village, Wickermoor. The tone is warm, wry and funny on the surface, with real dread and real grief underneath. The player controls a party of four chosen from six companions: Rook Coldwake, Tobin Hayward, Silas Vane, Delphine Ravelle, Lucan Houndstooth and Cordelia Skein. They are quirky, capable adults.

THE NARRATOR. A NARRATOR row is spoken by the Vagrant, the green-skinned ferryman of the ghost train, who tells the tale in a folksy Southern drawl. At the camp fire he is warm and wry, and when a talk turns sad his humour leaves and he goes plain and level. He speaks to the party as "you" and about the companion in the third person, by first name. Present tense, one or two sentences, under about 32 words. Concrete senses (a smell, a sound, a touch, what the hands are doing) over adjectives. Never tell the player what to feel. Never "suddenly". No facts the party could not see. Drop the final g ("hangin'") in about one Narrator row in four, and use no other dialect spelling. He is kind, never mocks a stumble and never makes light of the dead.

RULES FOR EVERY LINE.
1. The companion's voice sheet below comes first. Match its accent, pace, vocabulary and contractions, and the existing lines. Use a pet phrase at most twice in the whole reply and never twice in one talk. Never repeat or closely paraphrase a line already in the voice sheet or the note.
2. A SAY row is the companion speaking: one or two short sentences, under about 28 words. Never put three sentences in one row; start another row instead.
3. The party's options (OPTION rows) are under 12 words, in the plain voice of the party, work at any hour and in any weather, never name a hero, and are never rolls or checks. A reply must always answer the option it follows.
4. Canon limits. Use only the facts in the voice sheet and the note below. Do not invent a new named person, place, monster, event, object the companion carries, or piece of the companion's history. You may invent small, harmless habits, fondnesses, superstitions and turns of phrase, and the look of the fire and the night. Name no place that the note does not name. Never state a dark secret. You may come close to one and step back.
5. Nothing here is a game system: no dice, no checks, no points, no levels, no HP, no "approval", no menus talked about aloud. Plain punctuation only (commas, full stops, hyphens, apostrophes, question marks, quotation marks inside a line when someone is quoted). No em dashes, no semicolons, no brackets, no asterisks, no stage directions, no placeholders.
6. Humour comes from the character, never explained. The sad turn is plain and short.
7. Our own words. Nothing quoted from any book.

THIS REQUEST. Region banter for The Drowned Crossroads: 8 short exchanges between two or three companions, spoken as the party walks about this place. There are no Narrator rows, no options and no replies. Every row is a companion talking to another companion, never to the player.

HOW IT WORKS. When the party comes into an area, now and then one exchange plays as a few lines of chat between companions who happen to be in the party, once each. Only two or three of the six are ever in the party, so each exchange stands alone, mentions nobody else and needs no setup. Each one below is about what is in front of the party in one place at one moment of the story. Banter is funny first; one line in an exchange may turn honest, never more. The chat is about the place: what it looks and smells like, what is odd or sad or silly in it, and how each companion's trade, habits and fears meet it.

RULES.
1. Each exchange is 4 to 6 SAY rows, each a companion's single line (one or two short sentences, under about 28 words), alternating naturally between the speakers; every speaker listed speaks at least once.
2. Use only the facts in the attached cast sheets and the "In front of them" facts of that exchange. The "Story now" line is everything the party knows of the story: a remark must never run ahead of it (name a villain, a fight or a result only if the Story now line does). Never state or hint at any companion's past or secret, and never say what anyone's debt is. No new named people, places or monsters.
3. Pet words and phrases: each companion's at most once in an exchange, and never in two consecutive lines. Companions call each other by first name.
4. No two exchanges may share a joke or a topic, and no line may repeat a line in a cast sheet. Spread the topics: do not make every exchange about the same kind of thing.
5. Plain punctuation only (commas, full stops, hyphens, apostrophes, question marks, quotation marks). No em dashes, semicolons, brackets, asterisks or stage directions. No game terms. Our own words.
AVOID in this region: The green baize table where Silas's bet was taken is his own scene: nobody mentions a particular table, Silas's debt or his creditor. Silas and Delphine's three-card monte is theirs: do not stage it. The Grinning Sinner is not to be described beyond what the facts say.

THE EXCHANGES (in this order):
EXCHANGE 1: Rook + Lucan (speaker ids: rook_coldwake, lucan_houndstooth)
  Story now: The party is on the first night's trail through the bayou, on a dry hummock. Lucan's hound may be called Barnaby now and is known to fear thunder.
  In front of them: The Dry Hummock: A raised island of cypress roots in black water A raised island of cypress roots in black water: dry enough for a fire, if you do not mind what watches from the reeds. Parts of it: The Dry Hummock. Things to see: A bald cypress; Reeds; The camp fire on the hummock; A withered hand at the edge of the light.
EXCHANGE 2: Tobin + Silas (speaker ids: tobin_hayward, silas_vane)
  Story now: The party has come to the old battlefield, under a green fog.
  In front of them: The Old Battlefield: A green fog lies on the hummock where armed men and the dead met. Nothing here moves except what the fog moves. Parts of it: The Old Battlefield. Things to see: A bald cypress; Reeds; Bones and torn purple cloth; A smashed strongbox cart; A purple-and-black banner in the mud; The green fog.
EXCHANGE 3: Delphine + Cordelia (speaker ids: delphine_ravelle, cordelia_skein)
  Story now: The party has come to Murkwater Bend, the stilt town.
  In front of them: Murkwater Bend: A stilt town of lamplit shacks and rope bridges over black water, and a purple-and-black flag over a wooden fort. Murkwater Bend stands on stilts among bald cypress: shacks, boathouses and trader's stalls joined by swaying walkways, lanterns hung in moss, and at its heart a fort flying purple and black. Parts of it: The south gate; The boathouses; The fight pits; Traders' Row; The Mud Church; The Ferryman's mooring; Mama Pelletier's cookshack; The fort apron. Things to see: Murkwater Bend, lamplit on its stilts; The purple-and-black flag over the fort; Lyla Webb's stall: charms, jewellery and loose change; The sunk ring of the fight pits; The pit board, chalked with odds; The Mud Church's plank door; A coffin boat, tied at the mooring; Barrels of pickled things; Hanging nets and crab traps. People here: Lyla Webb; Mama Pelletier; Tibby Marsh.
EXCHANGE 4: Rook + Cordelia (speaker ids: rook_coldwake, cordelia_skein)
  Story now: The party is inside the Bayou King's fort, among the refugees.
  In front of them: The Bayou King's Fort: A palisade fort crowded with refugees, with a cramped throne hall of mismatched plush furniture. Inside the palisade a yard full of refugees, bandits in tribute and enforcers in purple and black. Beyond it a cramped throne hall of mismatched plush furniture and a cushioned chair by a window. Parts of it: The yard; The throne hall; The guest room. Things to see: The cushioned chair by the window; A bed that has seen worse nights; A plush sofa from three different houses; A rug that was a banner once; Bedrolls and a child's wooden boat. People here: Vander Boone; A refugee; An enforcer.
EXCHANGE 5: Tobin + Delphine (speaker ids: tobin_hayward, delphine_ravelle)
  Story now: The party has come into the Marshwinder shack.
  In front of them: The Marshwinder Shack: A one-room shack of trinkets under neon sigils, every tag marked 3 CP. Warm firelight from outside proves false. The room is cluttered with trinkets and bottles glowing neon green and magenta under sigils; carved idols and woven dolls crowd the shelves, each with a paper tag reading 3 CP. A spiral st... Parts of it: The shack. Things to see: A spiral stair into darkness; Bottles glowing magenta; A tag: 3 CP; A woven doll with your size of hands.
EXCHANGE 6: Tobin + Lucan (speaker ids: tobin_hayward, lucan_houndstooth)
  Story now: The party is at the lagoon, looking at the riverboat casino across the water. Lucan's hound may be called Barnaby now and is known to fear thunder.
  Talk about: its first look: what the party sees and smells on coming in.
  In front of them: Dead Man's Lagoon: A mangrove-ringed lake with a neon riverboat at its heart. A mangrove-ringed lake. At its centre a riverboat is moored, funnels coughing magenta, a gangplank down to a mud island. Heroes without a token see only a wreck, split in two, with part of an old name in faded paint. Parts of it: The landing; The mud island. Things to see: The lagoon, and what is moored in it; A wreck, split in two, with faded letters; Something steel glowing under the water.
EXCHANGE 7: Silas + Delphine (speaker ids: silas_vane, delphine_ravelle)
  Story now: The party has come aboard the riverboat casino and stands on its top deck.
  In front of them: The Dead Man's Hand: Promenade: The top decks of a ghostly riverboat casino, crowded with glassy-eyed revellers. Neon soulfire, green and magenta. The deck circles the ship, crowded with well-dressed revellers whose eyes will not quite meet yours, and holds the balcony over the hall. Catchy jazz comes from everywhere. Parts of it: Dead Man's Gangplank; The top deck; The balcony. Things to see: A black flag with a crocodile skull; A paddle wheel that never turns. People here: A bellhop; A reveler.
EXCHANGE 8: Tobin + Cordelia (speaker ids: tobin_hayward, cordelia_skein)
  Story now: The Grinning Sinner is dead. The party is back at the lagoon, with the casino quiet.
  Talk about: something different from the other exchange in this place: how it feels now.
  In front of them: Dead Man's Lagoon: A mangrove-ringed lake with a neon riverboat at its heart. A mangrove-ringed lake. At its centre a riverboat is moored, funnels coughing magenta, a gangplank down to a mud island. Heroes without a token see only a wreck, split in two, with part of an old name in faded paint. Parts of it: The landing; The mud island. Things to see: The lagoon, and what is moored in it; A wreck, split in two, with faded letters; Something steel glowing under the water.

THE ROW FORMAT (exact). One row per line:

EXCHANGE <number>
SAY <speaker id>: <line>
SAY <speaker id>: <line>
...

Use the speaker ids exactly as given (for example SAY rook_coldwake: ...). Write exactly 8 EXCHANGE blocks, numbered 1 to 8, and nothing else.

ATTACHED DOCUMENTS. Two documents come attached to this message; read both before you write: `tasks/crooked-moon-companions/banter-cast-1.md` (the voice sheets and fact lists for Rook Coldwake, Tobin Hayward and Silas Vane) and `tasks/crooked-moon-companions/banter-cast-2.md` (the same for Delphine Ravelle, Lucan Houndstooth and Cordelia Skein).
result:
EXCHANGE 1
SAY rook_coldwake: Poor drainage on this hummock, Lucan, and these cypress roots are buckled past all proper zoning. Whoever left a withered hand by the reeds never filed for burial.
SAY lucan_houndstooth: Hush now, the dark has teeth behind those reeds, if you please. Though I must deduct a mark from the quarry for leaving its extremities in the mud.
SAY rook_coldwake: Your Barnaby is crowding my boots again, and he is shaking worse than a loose headstone. Is there thunder coming, or did someone drop kettle corn in the fire?
SAY lucan_houndstooth: Good heavens, no, that yip is a grave omen of marsh predators, I assure you. Sit, Barnaby, stay close by the light while the watchman checks the perimeter.
SAY rook_coldwake: Mind the turf by that water, lad, the black mud goes down deep.Remind me to draw a breath before we turn in, or the damp will stiffen my ribs.

EXCHANGE 2
SAY silas_vane: Look at that smashed strongbox cart, Tobin, somebody folded hard when the dead called the bet. All that purple cloth in the mud and not a single copper left to palm.
SAY tobin_hayward: Leave the Mud alone, Silas, this green fog tastes of sour marrow and split iron. You breathe too much of that in and even my stitching won't hold your lungs.
SAY silas_vane: Good thing I don't keep lungs behind these ribs, friend, though the chill is rattling through my bones something fierce. Tell's in the twitch, and those reeds aren't moving on the wind.
SAY tobin_hayward: Nothing grows right where armed men rot under a banner, just bad seed and wet bone. Hold still, you've caught torn purple thread on your censer chain and it's fraying.
SAY silas_vane: Let it fray, I'd rather swing bitter herbs than linger where the house cleaned everybody out. Keep walking before that fog decides we owe on the old tab.

EXCHANGE 3
SAY delphine_ravelle: Look at these swaying walkways, Cordelia, a whole town hung on stilts like a cheap matinee set. One slip into that black water and my hem is ruined for the season.
SAY cordelia_skein: The structural ratio of rope to cypress is delightfully precarious, darling. More importantly, Mama Pelletier's barrels of pickled specimens by the cookshack suggest a fascinating local brine.
SAY delphine_ravelle: Your Foolishness just tried to rhyme coffin boat with petticoat, and I am ready to drop him in a crab trap. At least Lyla Webb's stall has a few shiny buttons worth the walk.
SAY cordelia_skein: Do examine the chalked odds on the fight pit board before you spend your loose change. The pathology of the crowd by the sunk ring indicates a very high mortality rate.
SAY delphine_ravelle: Cheap seats always want blood on the sawdust, darling, it is the oldest billing in the business. Let us keep to the lanterns before the damp unpicks my cuffs.

EXCHANGE 4
SAY rook_coldwake: This palisade is well past capacity, Cordelia, bedrolls blocking the yard and zero fire clearance. And that throne hall sofa looks cobbled together from three separate evictions.
SAY cordelia_skein: The upholstery is an anatomical marvel of bad stitching, Rook, though I am more intrigued by the refugees' pulses. Fear has elevated every heart rate in the yard by forty percent.
SAY rook_coldwake: You can leave their humours off the shift log, they have had a rough night without you tapping your vials. Someone even left a child's wooden boat by the rug.
SAY cordelia_skein: A former banner repurposed as floor covering, stained with bayou mud and mild arterial spray. Vander Boone's enforcers in purple and black clearly lack a proper sanitation assay.
SAY rook_coldwake: Unruly lot, the whole garrison, lounging in cushioned chairs while the drainage fails outside. Settle down now, let us finish our business and clear the yard.

EXCHANGE 5
SAY delphine_ravelle: Warm firelight through the window and then neon magenta bottles on the shelf, what a cheap trick for the gallery. Though at three coppers a tag, the house is practically giving the props away.
SAY tobin_hayward: Keep your fingers off the shelves, Delphine, the weave on these idols is twisted right against the grain. Whoever tied that reed work was stitching a canker straight into the straw.
SAY delphine_ravelle: Look at this woven doll on the end, Tobin, it has hands the exact size of mine. Tell me right now you did not leave one of your little poppets here.
SAY tobin_hayward: I don't work in marsh reed, girl, and I never tag my seams for three coppers. Step back from that spiral stair, the dark down there smells of wet burlap and old hexing.
SAY delphine_ravelle: He is not laughing over my shoulder anymore, Tobin, not a single pun. Let us get out of this shack before someone reaches for our threads.

EXCHANGE 6
SAY tobin_hayward: Funnels coughing magenta smoke into the mangroves, and the water tastes of drowned rust and sweet rot. That is no proper boat on the mud island, Lucan, it is a split wreck wearing paint.
SAY lucan_houndstooth: A fascinating glamour upon the quarry, Tobin, though the scent of river mud and scorched oil is most uncivilised. Even Barnaby has flattened his ears at that gangplank.
SAY tobin_hayward: My mice won't even poke their noses out of my lapels with that neon light on the water. Something steel is glowing down under the surface, right where the taproots rot.
SAY lucan_houndstooth: Prime specimen of an ambush snare, if you please, dressed up with faded letters to lure the unwary. I award it three out of ten for subtle posture.
SAY tobin_hayward: Good soil never held water that colour, and I don't trust a plank that looks whole from only one angle. Keep your lantern low and watch your footing on the mud.

EXCHANGE 7
SAY silas_vane: Green and magenta soulfire, catchy jazz, and a hundred glassy-eyed marks who won't look you in the socket. Watch your step on the promenade, Delphine, this whole top deck is a rigged shoe.
SAY delphine_ravelle: Mind the seams, darling, I know a papier-mache headliner when I walk across one. A paddle wheel that never turns and a crocodile skull on the flag, it is terribly overdone.
SAY silas_vane: That bellhop by the balcony hasn't blinked since we came up the gangplank, friend. Nobody here is playing for coins, and the house doesn't let the winners walk off the boat.
SAY delphine_ravelle: Look at the revellers' cuffs, Silas, fine clothes and not a single soul inside them awake enough to clap. It is just a stage full of puppets waiting for the curtain to drop.
SAY silas_vane: Then keep your hands out of your pockets and don't call the tune, darling. We take one look over the balcony and we fold before the music stops.

EXCHANGE 8
SAY cordelia_skein: Remarkable how quickly the magenta smoke dissipates from the funnels once the host pathology is excised. The ambient pulse of the entire lagoon has dropped to a flat zero.
SAY tobin_hayward: The rot hasn't left the mud island, Cordelia, it just went quiet under the mangroves. Look out past the landing, it is only a split wreck with faded letters now.
SAY cordelia_skein: My six eyes still register something steel glowing beneath the water, though the arcanum ratio is rapidly cooling. A pity, I had hoped to bottle a sample of that neon vapour.
SAY tobin_hayward: Leave it in the silt where it belongs, we don't need swamp humours corked in your waistcoat. The air still smells like scorched bone, and my straw is damp through.
SAY cordelia_skein: Your primrose at the cuff appears quite unbothered by the damp, darling. Come along, let us quit the landing before the mosquitoes discover you have no blood to assay.
